description: Declare alert rules in both deployment specs so a failure notifies a person. Neither spec has an alerts key, and the specs are applied on every deploy — the platform's create-time default alerts may already have been overwritten, so confirm the live spec before writing config. Production gets failed-deployment and failed-domain alerts plus restart-count and memory alerts on the backend service; staging gets failed-deployment only, because it declares no domain and utilisation noise on staging trains people to ignore the channel.
expectedBehavior: A failed deployment notifies a configured recipient in both environments

The backend service alerts on repeated restarts and on sustained high memory — the two signals that catch an out-of-memory kill on a 512 MB instance, which the liveness probe cannot catch because it is a static literal
Staging declares no domain alert, having no domain
The alert recipient is a real inbox, not an unattended address
verificationSteps: Fetch the live spec for each app and diff it against the committed spec; record any pre-existing drift before changing anything
Deploy, then fetch the live spec again and confirm the declared alert rules are present
Trigger a deliberately failing deploy on staging and confirm the notification arrives at the configured inbox
